To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sudden loss was common among clients with severe mental illness (SMI) and was significantly related to PTSD symptoms, even when controlling for other sources of traumatic stress.

sudden loss is a common occurrence in the lives of clients with severe mental illness, that distress from sudden loss is significantly associated with PTSD, and that distress from sudden losses accounts for unique and significant variance in PTSD symptoms over and above the variance explained by other sources of distress.

(1) the majority of community mental health clients with a severe mental disorder have experienced sudden losses in their lifetime, (2) the majority of these clients have experienced a sudden loss in the previous 6 months, (3) clients who experience a sudden loss in their lives are more likely to experience symptoms of PTSD, and (4) the distress associated with sudden loss accounts for unique variance in PTSD symptom severity over and above the distress associated with other types of traumatic events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the subjective distress associated with sudden loss in clients with severe mental illness.
the subjective experience of loss, and the impact of loss on the individual’s mental and physical health.
the impact of sudden interpersonal loss on clients with a severe mental disorder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“the results suggest that the sudden loss of a loved one is an important and unique risk factor for PTSD in individuals with SMI.”
sudden interpersonal loss is a common experience for individuals with severe mental illness and is associated with significant distress and symptoms of posttraumatic stress.
the sudden loss of a friend or loved one can have an adverse effect on the psychological well-being of clients with severe mental illness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sudden losses in the lives of clients with a severe mental disorder are common and are associated with PTSD symptoms.
sudden loss of a loved one is a significant predictor of PTSD in clients with severe mental illness.
sudden losses are common in the lives of clients with severe mental illness and that distress related to such losses can be an important source of trauma-related symptomatology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
practitioners should routinely assess interpersonal loss among clients with SSMI and offer brief interventions aimed at helping clients manage such losses.

the experience of sudden loss of a loved one is associated with PTSD symptoms in clients with a SMI and that this association is not accounted for by the presence of a comorbid Axis I or Axis II disorder.

practitioners should be aware of and assess the subjective distress that clients with severe mental illness may experience from sudden losses in their interpersonal relationships, and practitioners should be prepared to offer brief, focused interventions that help clients cope with such sudden interpersonal losses.
